# M0-3: Slack Socket Mode spike

- Milestone: M0
- Branch / worktree: `t/M0-3`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M0-3`
- Depends on: none (BA-2 done)
- Touches (exclusive while running): `spikes/slack/`, `docs/build/spikes/slack.md`
- Plan refs: architecture.md §5 (Slack); requirements.md R9b only
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no

## Goal
Prove the Slack building blocks finbot needs, end to end, from a throwaway Go program on this Mac: Socket Mode connection,
posting to the private channel, Block Kit buttons with the click received, threaded replies received, and Slack user id →
identity. The output is a findings doc, not product code.

## Setup facts (verified by sup)
- The app "finbot" is in workspace Ashton Clan. Socket Mode is on and token rotation is off.
- `.env` has `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` (`xapp-`, works with `apps.connections.open`) and `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` (`xoxb-`). Bot scopes:
  `chat:write, channels:history, channels:read, users:read, groups:read, groups:history, groups:write`. Never print either
  token.
- Channel: **private `#finbot-finances`**, bot is a member. Resolve its id at runtime with `users.conversations`; don't
  hard-code or commit it.
- Bot events: `message.channels` is configured. `message.groups` (needed for a private channel) may or may not be. Verify
  it; if events from the channel don't arrive, report it as a QUESTION signal for Brendan to add it, rather than working
  around it.

## Scope
- A program under `spikes/slack/` (its own `go.mod`; root module untouched) using `github.com/slack-go/slack` and its
  `socketmode` package.
- Connect over Socket Mode. Log connection events. Ack envelopes correctly.
- Post one test message to `#finbot-finances`: a mock "categorize this?" question with top-3 category buttons plus
  "other…", using a **fake** transaction (e.g. "TEST: Costco $12.34"). Clearly label everything as a spike test.
- Receive the `block_actions` click and record the shape: user id, action id/value, message ts, channel. Then update the
  message to show the choice.
- Receive a threaded reply to that message (`message` event with `thread_ts`), and record the event shape.
- Slack user id → identity: `users.info` → name / real name / email (whether email is available with current scopes). Map
  the two humans in the channel to a stub "users" table in memory.
- Brendan has to click a button and post a threaded reply. When ready, append `QUESTION M0-3: please click a button and
  reply in thread on the TEST message in #finbot-finances` to your signal file, and wait (poll your own log, don't spin).
- Measure the click → event latency and reconnect behaviour: kill the socket and verify it reconnects.
- Write `docs/build/spikes/slack.md`:
  - findings labeled VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED;
  - the exact scopes and events needed (including whether `groups:write` is unnecessary and can be dropped);
  - a recommendation;
  - an "Impact on architecture" section (§5).

## Out of scope
- Any YNAB access. LLM/claude handling of free text (§5a, that's M0-4/M5). DMs beyond noting whether they need extra
  scopes (`im:*`).
- Posting more than ~5 messages, or to any channel other than `#finbot-finances`. Mentioning `@channel`/`@here`.
- Committing tokens, channel/user ids, emails or real names. Use placeholders in the doc.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] `cd spikes/slack && go run .` connects over Socket Mode and posts the test message (show the log lines, ids
      redacted).
- [ ] A real button click and a real threaded reply were received; their payload shapes are in the doc.
- [ ] `docs/build/spikes/slack.md` has labeled findings, the required scopes and events, a recommendation and an Impact
      section.
- [ ] The branch diff contains no tokens, ids, emails or names (grep it and show the check).
- [ ] Root `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` still green.
